paras: The killing of John Randolph was the fatal stabbing of a Black man during a row at a frolic at Tobe Duke's farm in Jackson County, Georgia, on the night of Tuesday, 1 February 1881. Three brothers named Hemphill were said to have killed Randolph and gravely wounded a second man, John Tate, and two of them were arrested. The killing drew only brief notices, one in a Georgia weekly and one in an Atlanta dispatch printed in Nebraska.

According to the Atlanta dispatch, "the negroes of the neighborhood" had gathered for a frolic at Tobe Duke's farm in Jackson County. Neither report gives the race of the Hemphill brothers or any cause for the quarrel.

During the night a row broke out, in which, by the dispatch's account, three Hemphill brothers killed Randolph and "probably mortally wounded" Tate. The Marietta Journal said that Randolph died by a knife "in the hands of Russ Hemphill, it is said," and that Russ was assisted by his brothers Edmund Hemphill and Allen Duke. Tate was carried to his home in a very critical condition.

By 4 February Tate was still alive, and two of the Hemphills were under arrest. The third brother, "known as Allen Duke," had "given leg bail," that is, fled. No report of an inquest, an indictment, a trial or Tate's fate appears in the coverage.

The Marietta Journal of 3 February printed the killing as a single sentence among unrelated Georgia items, naming Randolph only as "a negro." Two days later the Omaha Daily Bee carried a fuller Atlanta special under the headline "Fatal Frolic," between short dispatches on a Virginia murder and a Nashville death. Both items treated the killing as routine crime news, without comment on the people involved or on race beyond the descriptive labels.

The Marietta Journal placed the killing on Tuesday night, while the Atlanta dispatch dated 4 February said the frolic took place "last night." Because the Journal had the story in its 3 February issue, the Tuesday date of 1 February is the better supported of the two.

bases: Both reports describe a killing by three named brothers during a 'row' at a frolic of Black neighbors, not a mob or a white attack; no race is given for the Hemphills (A1, A2).

The Marietta Journal brief and the Atlanta dispatch printed in the Omaha Daily Bee agree that the Hemphill brothers killed John Randolph in Jackson county, with differing detail that suggests separate reporting (A1, A2).

accounts.label: Atlanta dispatch
accounts.gist: During a row at a frolic of the neighborhood's Black residents at Tobe Duke's farm, three Hemphill brothers killed Randolph and probably mortally wounded John Tate; two were arrested and the third fled.

framing.detail: The Marietta Journal ran the killing as one line among unrelated Georgia items, identifying Randolph only as 'a negro'.
The Omaha Daily Bee printed the Atlanta special under 'Fatal Frolic' among other short Southern dispatches.

versions.value: 'last night' in a dispatch dated 4 February (3 February)

conflicts.note: The Marietta Journal of 3 February already carried the killing, so it cannot have happened on the night of 3 February; the Atlanta dispatch's 'last night' is probably loose and Tuesday 1 February is better supported.
